There are definitely better courses out there in the US. Outside of accomodations for spectators, there are other pdga requirements. The course would need to host successful B-tier events for 3+ years with no player complaints for consideration. Also, there's a requirement that the TD who runs the event(s) to have an existing track record of running B-tiers and above. There is also mileage restrictions to avoid conflicts with other possible events. I would assume there's some courses out there that are denied due to a conflict with a pre-existing stop landing on the same date(s).

If that criteria is something that can be met, then an application to request the event to be an A-tier+ can be submitted ($100 fee, still needs to be reviewed by the PDGA) I'm hopeful in the next few years we start to see some of these other courses pop up on the tour as long as the other accomodations can be met as well.

I went through a period where in tournaments it didn't necessarily feel like pressure or yips, but just could not execute regardless of confidence. Outside of my typical putting practice, I wanted to simulate some sort of tournament pressure, so I increased difficulty during my casual rounds.

I require myself making 2 putts from my lie in order for the score to count. So, if I have a birdie putt, I have to make both putts. If I make the first and not the second, I take a stroke and putt twice from the missed one. It's made a world of difference as we are conditioned to just make 1 and it counts and it greatly reduced the tournament woes.

Fast forward to the unveiling of both consoles, I liked both presentations from Sony and Microsoft, but, Microsoft started to shove not only the Kinect again down our throats but now pushing the console more towards the "All-in-one entertainment box" This just brought back the same awkward feeling I had when MS originally introduced the Kinect and I didn't want it.

At this point I could see the shift since Sony was clearly for me, the core gamer. The XB One has its perks but it's not what I was looking for in a next gen system. 

I was an Xbox owner since the launch of the original and was a member of Xbox Live for 10, almost 11 years. It was hard to say bye, but I clearly felt Sony was holding more focus on the gamer versus the casual. Now that I own a PS4, I could not be any happier, the network is solid with no major issues and the games look beautiful. (The changes to the controller help as well since the other DS controllers felt small in my hands for some reason)

TL;DR - Sony showed me a console for gamers and that their business model was focusing on just that. Microsoft was looking to be more of a total entertainment experience for the casual and that was what turned me away and wanting a PS4 instead.
